posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Bunker fills a niche.  He isn't a go-to hero, he isn't going to carry the team unless he has the right help and he isn't a jack of all trades that can fill out a team and make up for that teams weaknesses.

Bunker is unable to fill a specific role even in damage, because of the unreliability of his build.  Almost every other hero has an easier time getting going than Bunker.  

AZ has 10 cards that let you use a power to deal damage the turn the card is played , Wraith has 12,  Expat has 14, and Arsenal access has a decent chance to as well,  Bunker has 6.

One shots that deal damage (without requiring other cards already being played to do so):

Bunker has 3, same as Wraith and Omnitron-X.

Argent Adept, Expat (unload and RPG require other cards to do damage), have zero.  Out of 18 heroes 13 have more one-shot damage cards than Bunker, if you count the cards that require other cards to be destroyed to deal damage everyone but Adept has more one-shots that deal damage than Bunker.

So given any situation where you only had cards in your hand to rely on doing damage that turn bunker has 9 cards that could work, same as Legacy and the Visionary.

As for direct impact on the match, Bunker has 16 cards that affect something other than himself.  24 of his cards don't deal damage, boost allies, or affect any deck or cards but his own.  Legacy, with all his self buffs has 24 that affect other decks.

What is the point of this info?

Bunker more than any other hero (depending on how you judge Fixer) has a deck that focuses on him.  Healing, reducing damage, mode cards, getting cards from the trash, drawing more cards, using more powers.  Even his base power only affects himself.

With that kind of focus on himself, and 15 cards focused on getting more cards in your hand and in play Bunker plays slower than most heroes.

That is insane.  Crono has one of the fastest decks in the game, and his cards almost all do damage.  Ammo Drop, Recharge Mode, Upgrade Mode, Decomissioned Hardware, Auxiliary power supply all are designed to get cards into your hand and in play, and yet they don't have any decent synergy.

Bunker isn't a jack-of-all-trades, master of none, he's an exercise in finding order in chaos.  He has too much stuff he can do, but it all depends on what you get, and whether those cards work together well.  When you get the right cards and can get into a groove early it is great to be bunker, but often you are left to make due with what you have.

Is that true of anyone, yes anyone can get a bad hand, but no one has as many no-impact cards as Bunker, 60% of his deck affects no one but him.  And those 24 cards involve exactly Zero that can pull an equipment card from your deck.  He has zero deck shrinking cards, all his extra draws require something to happen to get the cards, use a power, wait a round, have a villain target destroyed.

Bunker ends up Clunky and slow, but powerful if he can get to that point.

Bunker isn't a bad hero, and I like the thematics of a not-perfect armored suit that is clunky and difficult to operate.  This isn't Iron Man, Vance isn't in a sleek efficient high-powered armor suit.  He can still pack a punch, or take a punch pretty dang well, and with the right cards can do both at the same time.

That's why I allow people to use my house ruled Mode card changes.  it gives a bit more flow to the mode cards, and gives a pull from your deck option (that has the one round delay to use that keeps with his deck mechanics).  It ends up usually speeding up Bunker's deck by 1-3 cards a game, or roughly the value of an Impromptu Invention getting played, and that makes a big difference with Bunker.

Overall I like him, I like the thematic side of him, and I enjoy playing him, esp. with some card support (Adept, Omni are amazing,Visionary and Fixer help him a lot as well)

If you play 4 heroes with two players play Omnitron-X and Bunker and have Omni throw Bunker a lot of Timeshifts, man it is fun.  There is a fan made alternate card on BGG with a similar power to Omni, you reveal the top two cards of your deck, put one into play and discard the other.  I'm not a fan (since I like the Mode card theme and it lessens the value of them) but it is an option for people that would like to drop into turret mode and still be able to get cards into play.

posts.name: Zed
posts.cooked:
I would not consider Bunker a generalist at all because, as phantaskippy pointed out, he is much too self focused. He nearly completely lacks any control or support aspects in the game.

He cannot remove ongoings/environments, he can't heal allies, give allies extra plays, retrieve from trash, give allies extra powers, re-order decks, give allies draws or do anything at all that interacts with other heroes.

In fact the ONLY card he has that I would consider to be control/support is Adhesive Foam Grenades. This near complete self focus should mean, logically, that he would have very high outgoing damage/survivability. I don't find this to be the case with even Tempest having the cards on hand to be as tanky as Bunker.

Tempest on the other hand, is quite possibly the most generally powerful character in the game; especially with anyone boosting his damage.

He has the most powerful mass damage in the game with many of his attacks hitting every non-hero character, a large number of massive damage one-shots, environment AND ongoing destruction, massive card draw, the best heal power in the game, Gene Bound Shackles to cream the main villain (combine with Vicious Cyclone for extra giggles), a damage reduction card, can retrive cards from the trash for the entire team, and finally is the only hero that can throw a card in play onto the top of the villain deck.

The sheer amount of insane utlity that Tempest brings to the table for any situation on top of the best mass damage in the game (and single target damage to nearly rival Ra) makes him easily the most versatile, and probably also the most powerful, hero in the game.

Tempest is the one hero above all I don't bring if I want a difficult game. Combine him with Legacy and most villains will simply melt, almost regardless of what you draw on Legacy/Tempest.

The best way I can describe Bunker is as a workhorse (echoing Drakossozh's statements).  He's survivable.  He's got Ok damage.  He mops up whatever is left, and creates openings for other people.  He takes the hits, sacrifices equipment, and keeps on going.

I don't take issue with the idea that Bunker is a solid hero, and doesn't need improved.

I do take issue with anyone claiming he is versatile in comparison to other heroes.

His effect on the game is relegated to dealing damage, taking damage and Adhesive Foam Grenades.  Ra can boost everyone's damage and make heroes immune to fire damage, Ra has more cards that affect the game (outside of himself) without dealing damage than Bunker does.

Bunker's Versatility comes soleley from being able to heal, take reduced damage and deal damage in various creative ways.

Bunker's strength over a Haka is that he can deal more instances of damage, which is his true strength.  But even then he can be matched pretty easily, you trade set up time and versatility for a reliable amount of damage at the end, for as long as his setup lasts.

Wraith and Bunker deal similar damage, Wraiths 4 card damage setup and Bunkers 3 cards setup give Wraith a 2 point damage advantage, at the cost of one extra turn, if you go five cards with Bunker you can get Ammo Drop and Gatling and outdamage Wraith by one, but Wraith still plays and draws cards at that point.  Letting her provide more versatile actions, as well as prepare to recover from any disaster.

Once Turret mode hits the field Bunker is done, he is what he is, and if he gives up Turret to adjust his setup he loses much of his power.

When you have the right cards he's pretty dang good, and really fits the "gets things done" title.  The problem is he is more susceptible to a hand that doesn't do anything to further the match at all than anyone else is.

I should clarify:

Long Setup is a poor choice of words.  Bunker is a slow starter, as he has no base power damage and no way to search for Grenade Launcher, Flak Cannon, or Gatling Gun.  He is more susceptible to a slow start than other heroes, even Expatriette or AZ.

Once you get a few key cards out you have to choose when to throw down turret mode.  Since he isn't doing much else to help the team than deal damage, you do need to do that at some point.  Omnicannon/Gatling is cool, esp. if you have recharge and plating out, but other than that you are looking for that 2 powers a turn and +1 damage.

Once you throw Turret you are done setting up.

When you destroy Turret you lose +1 and a power use, to play cards that aren't going to make an impact that turn.  It is a rare time when not doing stuff now to do more later works well in Sentinels, plus at the time you are ditching Turret to play more cards you aren't early in a match anymore, usually it is better to stay in turret and help finish the deal.

Because of this Bunker usually falls into a few patterns in his matches:

1.  Never get set up, but do pretty good anyway.

2.  Get a great setup, but almost too late to really shine with it.

3.  Lucky opening hand and early draws gets you rolling early with a small card setup, and you lock into it for the rest of the game.

Unless you have extra card plays early/Omnitron-X helping you out.  If there is support Bunker can be the only damage dealer, but if he gets a rotten shuffle it isn't going to go well.

posts.cooked:
While I am a big fan of Bunker as is, IF I had to change something it would be Gatling Gun. Gatling Gun  is a really cool card in that it changes Bunker's base power from drawing a card to dealing damage. The problem is, is that as a damage power, it is simply worse than Flak Cannon  or Grenade Launcher .

If I had all three of those cards in my hand, I wouldn't put down Gatling gun first. If, however, it was comparable, I might. Playing Flak Cannon or Grenade Launcher not only puts you closer to Turret Mode, but it also moves you away from Recharge and Upgrade Mode. This not only makes those cards less desirable, but it also takes away from the different paths. However, if it is worth it to play Gatling Gun, this could change.

In fact, by making Gatling Gun bigger, you also don't have to rely on Turret Mode as much. You can use a combination of Gatling Gun & Flak Cannon/Gatling Gun & Grenade Launcher while not having a mode. This will stall your deck as you aren't getting an cards, but you can enter faster and without Turret Mode. If setup properly Turret Mode is still better, which still leaves that option.

You don't have to worry about Turret Mode being too powerful with the buff from Gatling Gun, because you would still need Ammo Drop to consistently pay the cost. However, if you can play all those cards, you would get the added Boost that a 5 card combo should have.

This would also make Recharge Mode more worth it. 2 damage doesn't really do anything (It can only kill birds and zombies outright). By making the damage worth it, there would be more of an incentive to enter tank mode and draw a lot of cards. You would change Recharge Mode from being draw 3 cards, to draw 2 cards and use a power.

There is also the issue of what to do with those extra cards from Recharge Mode. All you really need are the cards for a Turret Mode setup. If you draws those quickly, great. If not, you are stuck with dead cards unless you find GG or Omni-Cannon. However, for only 2 damage a card, it usually isn't worth it. By making GG better, you can keep digging for it, and not feel like you wasted your turns.

Once you draw those cards, you want to use Upgrade Mode to play them fast. Upgrade Mode grants you 2 plays and a draw. As it is, you can try to rely on that draw and exit Recharge Mode earlier and hope for the best. If you stayed in Recharge Mode to find all the cards you need, you really don't need the extra draw from Upgrade Mode. With Gatling Gun, you can change that draw into a power. By buffing the power, you can make it worth it to stay in Upgrade Mode longer and get more cards out

So what sort of change should Gatling Gun have? You could make the power different depending on which Mode Bunker is in, but that could get complicated and require a lot of text. The simplest solution would be to make it deal 3 damage instead of 2. This would at least make it comparable to Flak Cannon, although not better.

You could also make it deal 4 damage. This would actually give more strategy outside of Turret Mode. Purposely going into Recharge mode to fuel a 4 damage Gatling Gun, can be very effective. The biggest issue, though, is that it would be better than Omni-Cannon, but a small buff to that might not be a bad idea either.

A third option is to give Gatling Gun an ability that Bunker doesn't have. For example, deal 1 damage to all non-hero targets. This could be powerful, but it might not make Gatling as strong in Recharge mode or Upgrade Mode, while making it stronger in Turret Mode, which is something we want to avoid.

phantaskippy:

At the start of your turn you may return this card to your hand, if you do you may play a mode card.

Internet was down at work so I fooled a bit with Vassal, doing some "let's see what I draw" and one game against Blade and two against Voss (you can do really quick solo games in Vassal).

I don't think it makes him as powerful as you say phanta. This rule encourages opening with Turret (never with Upgrade, sometimes with Recharge for the damage reduction) with another Mode in hand. Opening with Turret plain trades a card draw for a power and then you just switch around with the modes mitigating the first turn "penalty" Upgrade/Recharge have. But this still makes you have turns of no-damage. The switch from Turret to Upgrade, play card and go back to Turret is like a cheat, sure. But that's it. Bunker's still has a slow start as a Hero, he still likes to draw lots of cards (discards hurt your potential) and he still is equipment dependant. My impression is that he is somewhat near Haka's power level and style: draw lot's of cards for conversion, get the right equipment/ongoing down and he might outshine other overall stronger heroes or do as good as the weaker ones. Wraith is still better IMO, she can still do more with equal or less time: stack Villain deck, reduce it's damage and/or deal as much damage (outside of OmniCannon). Would need to try him against other Villains with destruction like La Capitan or Omnitron.
If you want a watered down version of this you might as well keep the no-destruction but have the Mode be played in your Play phase. It's not as interesting or good switching Modes but you keep a higher card count.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I have opened with upgrade, that extra card play is still great, esp. if you have several of Plating, Ammo, Auxiliary, Gatling or Omni+recharge.  You get them out and then switch to recharge or turret.  I only go turret right off the bat if I get ammo drop or really need to deal the damage.

With the start of turn switch out getting more cards is a bigger priority, since you can use them even better.

Upgrade to Recharge is a great switch, play upgrade, and a card, play two more the next turn, if you don't have anything going still start of turn switch to recharge and you get the three cards that turn, and when you switch back to upgrade you don't waste a play on upgrade.

The more you use modes that fit what you can do with your hand, the more cards you gain with this house rule.

Using Recharge and Upgrade to get cards and then put them in play is a real bonus with this rule, as you don't lose a card play, the mode, or the first draw of recharge.

Bunker can get to a basic Turret-Mode setup slightly quicker than regular, but the big thing is you can upgrade from that setup to a really awesome one so much quicker.

You can also simply return a style to hand and not play another one, you just have to then play a mode card to get going again.

You are still susceptible to a really bad opening, but once you get a little bit going it helps speed the rpocess a lot.

Also putting Bunker with Wraith was probably a reach, but I find this house rule turns him into one of the best damage dealers, and his tanking.
